_note: Per-state rule profiles. lsv/golf_cart: max_posted = highest posted mph allowed; designated_only = only cart paths + designated roads; assume_designated = OSM highway classes treated as designated where the region says so (UNVERIFIED unless sourced); radius_mi = max distance from home/registration; daylight_only; cross = may cross faster roads at intersections. golf_cart = plain golf cart / PTV / motorized cart (no VIN-based FMVSS 500 compliance); lsv = street-legal low-speed vehicle / NEV. not_street_legal = plain golf carts may not use public roads (cart paths only). The app's vehicle toggle picks which profile applies (public/roadrule.js).

golf_cart.cite: CVC 21716 (golf carts only on highways posted ≤25 mph, within a business/residence district); CVC 21115 + Streets & Highways Code §1950-1965 golf cart transportation plans may designate other routes

F.S. 316.212(1) (golf carts only on roads a county/city has designated and signed, based on speed and traffic); 316.212(6)-(8) daylight unless equipped; 316.2126 municipal use. FLHSMV/FDOT guidance cites designated roads posted ≤30 mph; app uses the designation (≤35) and flags this. UNCONFIRMED

O.C.G.A. 40-6-331 (PTVs only where a local ordinance allows); app uses the common local cap of ≤25 mph (Glynn County, Tybee, Peachtree City streets except Hwy 74/54/Peachtree Pkwy). UNCONFIRMED per town

lsv.cite: S.C. Code 56-2-100 (a low speed vehicle may use a highway posted 35 mph or less and may cross a faster highway at an intersection)

golf_cart.cite: S.C. Code 56-2-90 (2025 Act No. 64, H.3292, eff. May 22, 2025; amended by 2026 Act No. 164, S.222, Section 6.A, eff. May 18, 2026): without a local ordinance, a permitted golf cart may use a secondary highway posted 35 mph or less, in daylight, within 4 miles of the registration address or of a gated-community entrance, and may cross a faster road at an intersection. A city or county may set hours, methods and locations by ordinance, still only on highways posted 35 mph or less, and may allow night driving with working headlights and taillights. A half-mile window around certain large athletic events is not drawn on the map.

lsv.cite: Tex. Transp. Code 551.303 (a neighborhood electric vehicle may use a street or highway posted 45 mph or less, may cross a faster road at an intersection, and may not travel faster than 35 mph; the map plans on roads posted 35 mph or less)

golf_cart.cite: Tex. Transp. Code 551.402 through 551.405 (license plate required, 551.402; daytime on a road posted 35 mph or less within 5 miles of where the cart is parked, and only to or from a golf course, 551.403; or in a master-planned community or on a beach open to vehicles; or where a city or an eligible county authorizes, 551.404; may cross a faster road at an intersection, 551.405)

lsv.cite: Single app rule ≤35 (Code of Ala. 32-1-1.1 LSV); Gulf Shores/Orange Beach region cap ≤25 (regions.json rule)

golf_cart.cite: No state golf-cart road statute; local ordinance (Gulf Shores Sec. 21-13, Orange Beach Sec. 70-273: streets ≤25 mph)
Arizona: golf carts must be registered/insured to use public streets; local police guidance (e.g. Marana PD) allows streets ≤35 mph. Sun City: A.R.S. 28-721(C) keep right. UNCONFIRMED

lsv.cite: ORC 4511.214 (under-speed/LSV on ≤35 roads where locally authorized; Put-in-Bay village permits carts)

golf_cart.cite: ORC 4511.214 (under-speed vehicles on roads ≤35 mph where the local authority allows; titled, inspected, plated); Put-in-Bay Codified Ord. 490.02

lsv.cite: N.C.G.S. 20-121.1 (LSV ≤35); golf carts by local ordinance (G.S. 160A-300.6)

golf_cart.note: golf cart rules vary by town (Duck ≤25, Nags Head ≤35, Kill Devil Hills: LSVs only)
golf_cart.cite: N.C.G.S. 160A-300.6 / 153A-245 (golf carts only where a town/county ordinance allows); app uses the most common cap of ≤25. UNCONFIRMED per town

lsv.note: street-legal electric LSVs (NEVs) only, max 25 mph; plain golf carts aren't street-legal in Hawaii
lsv.cite: HRS 291C-134 (neighborhood electric vehicles: roads posted ≤35 mph, may cross at intersections, no controlled-access highways); HRS 291C-53

golf_cart.note: plain golf carts aren't street-legal in Hawaii. Switch to LSV if yours is a registered NEV
golf_cart.cite: HRS 291C-134 (only neighborhood electric vehicles), HRS 286-2 (golf carts not registrable motor vehicles)

lsv.note: registered LSVs only; plain golf carts aren't road-legal in Maine
lsv.cite: 29-A M.R.S. §2089 (LSVs on roads posted ≤35 mph, may cross at intersections); §501(2-A) golf carts only on islands without state roads

golf_cart.note: plain golf carts aren't road-legal in Maine. Switch to LSV if yours is a registered LSV
golf_cart.cite: 29-A M.R.S. §501(2-A) (golf carts only on islands without state roads); §2089 LSVs

lsv.note: NJ LSVs may use roads posted 25 mph or less; a town, county or NJDOT can open roads up to 35 mph or ban LSVs
lsv.cite: N.J.S.A. 39:4-31.1 / NJ MVC low-speed vehicles (roads posted 25 mph or less; may cross faster roads at intersections)

golf_cart.note: plain golf carts aren't street-legal in New Jersey; only FMVSS 500 LSVs with NJ title, registration and insurance. Switch to LSV if yours is one
golf_cart.cite: NJ MVC low-speed vehicles: an LSV must meet 49 CFR 571.500 and be titled, registered and insured; golf carts don't qualify

lsv.note: not on dual highways (Coastal Hwy) outside towns except to cross
lsv.cite: 21 Del. C. §2113A (LSVs on roads posted 35 mph or less; not on dual highways in unincorporated areas except to cross)

golf_cart.note: Delaware DMV: golf carts are not allowed on Delaware highways. Switch to LSV if yours is a registered LSV
golf_cart.cite: Delaware DMV special vehicles: golf carts are not allowed to operate on Delaware highways

lsv.cite: Va. Code §46.2-908.3 (LSVs on highways posted 35 mph or less)

golf_cart.cite: Va. Code §46.2-916.3 (golf carts only on highways the locality designates, posted 25 mph or less; cross at intersections posted 35 or less; sunrise to sunset unless equipped)

lsv.note: A town traffic authority or the Office of State Traffic Administration can prohibit LSVs on a road under its control
lsv.cite: Conn. Gen. Stat. Sec. 14-289m (P.A. 24-20, effective Oct. 1, 2024): LSVs on highways with an established speed limit of 25 mph or less, unless the local traffic authority or OSTA prohibits them

golf_cart.note: Plain golf carts are not street-legal unless that town's traffic authority permits them. Switch to LSV if yours is registered.
golf_cart.cite: Conn. Gen. Stat. Sec. 14-300g: a traffic authority may permit golf carts in daylight only, on roads posted 25 mph or less, with a horn, flag, and a licensed driver

lsv.note: A titled, registered low-speed vehicle. A plain golf cart is a different rule and needs a city resolution.
lsv.cite: MCL 257.660(8): a low-speed vehicle must not be operated on a street with a speed limit of more than 35 mph, except to cross that street. MDOT may prohibit one on a state highway for safety.

golf_cart.note: Plain golf carts are not street-legal unless that city, village, or township has adopted a resolution. Switch to LSV if yours is titled and registered.
golf_cart.cite: MCL 257.657a: a city under 65,000 may allow golf carts only by resolution, only on streets posted 30 mph or less, not from half an hour before sunset to half an hour after sunrise, and not on a state trunk line except to cross

lsv.note: Madison's ordinance allows this. A different Wisconsin town needs its own check.
lsv.cite: Wis. Stat. 349.26 (a municipality may allow a low-speed vehicle on a roadway posted 35 mph or less). WisDOT TEOpS 13-3-1: where no ordinance applies, local roads posted 35 mph or less.

golf_cart.note: Plain golf carts need a municipal ordinance. Madison's low-speed vehicle section does not grant that.
golf_cart.cite: Wis. Stat. 349.18(1m): a municipality may allow golf carts on highways posted 25 mph or less. Without that ordinance, a golf cart is not a low-speed vehicle.

lsv.note: Registered, insured, and inspected. A city may prohibit a road and must post that ban.
lsv.cite: R.I. Gen. Laws 31-19.6-1: a registered low-speed vehicle may use a public highway posted 35 mph or less, and may cross a highway posted 35 to 45 mph at a signal or stop sign

golf_cart.note: A golf cart is not an LSV and is not registered for Rhode Island public roads. Switch to LSV if yours is factory-certified.
golf_cart.cite: R.I. Gen. Laws 31-19.6-1 and the RI DMV: a golf cart is not manufactured to the low-speed vehicle standard and may not be registered as one
